title: SDK Runtime Recovery Patterns and Idempotency Conventions — defaults & taxonomy playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines a cross-language playbook for sensible SDK defaults and conventions around retries, backoff, idempotency keys, and a retryable-error taxonomy. Scope: Python, TypeScript, Go SDKs for Redwood API (generation, chat, embeddings, streaming). Goal is to provide predictable out-of-the-box behavior that minimizes duplicate side effects, simplifies streaming recovery, and reduces incidents caused by inconsistent client retry logic.
deliverables: Canonical retry/backoff default config for non-streaming and streaming calls (per-language knobs)
Standard idempotency key behavior and header conventions with example integrations
Retryable error taxonomy mapping to HTTP/gRPC codes and model/runtime error codes
Cross-SDK test harness and chaos-fault scenarios (network flakiness, server 5xx, partial stream interruptions)
Migration guide + opt-in grace period + telemetry plan to measure retry side effects
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs implement the default config and expose the same ergonomic APIs for overrides
Integration tests demonstrate correct dedup for idempotent operations and safe behavior for non-idempotent ops
Streaming client resumes or fails in documented, deterministic ways in response to transient errors
Operational telemetry (retries, duplicate suppression rate, user-visible error rate) surfaces in Console dashboards
Documentation and migration guide published under SDK docs; deprecation warnings absent until opt-in window closes
decisions: Default max_retries: non-streaming idempotent requests = 3, non-idempotent requests = 0 (no automatic retry). Rationale: preserve safety-first behavior while reducing transient failures for idempotent client patterns.
Backoff: jittered exponential backoff with initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=5s. Use 'full jitter' to avoid thundering herd.

Streaming: connection-level reconnect allowed for specific transient error classes; server-provided resume tokens used where supported. Client will attempt a single reconnect (max_reconnects=1) with backoff of 500ms before surfacing failure.

Idempotency keys: SDKs will expose an optional 'idempotency_key' parameter. When provided, SDK sets header 'x-rd-idempotency-key'. SDKs will not auto-generate for non-idempotent operations; higher-level helpers (e.g., retries.with_idempotency()) will optionally synthesize keys for safe retry wrappers.

Retryable error taxonomy: base on HTTP/gRPC semantics + runtime error codes. 429, 502, 503, 504 are retryable (with attention to idempotency). 5xx server errors generally retryable for safe ops. 409/422 are client-state errors and not retried. Network timeouts/connectivity errors are retryable. Model-specific 'overloaded'/'timeout' runtime codes classified as retryable; 'invalid prompt' or 'quota_exceeded' NOT retryable.

Telemetry: SDK emits structured events for retry attempts, final outcome, and idempotency key used (hashed) to allow de-dup tracking without leaking keys. This is enabled by default for hosted usage; in Private deployments telemetry respects customer settings.
comments: 2025-02-10 Asha Patel: Kickoff — consolidated inputs from SDK leads (Python: Mira, TS: Jonas, Go: Priya). Initial proposal drafted after triage. Linked design notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/sdk-retries-playbook

2025-02-12 Diego Morales: Implementation spike completed for Python. Verified backoff parameters with synthetic 503 injection; default of 3 retries reduced transient error surface by ~72% in load testing.

2025-02-13 Mira Chen (Python SDK): Found an edge case where streaming reconnect + idempotency leads to duplicates for append-like operations. Added requirement: SDK must expose 'stream_resume_token' to server and provide opt-out behaviour for append semantics.

2025-02-14 Jonas Berg (TS SDK): TypeScript ergonomics proposed: top-level RetryPolicy class + fluent builder. We agreed to keep a small surface: simple kwargs and a RetryPolicy object for advanced use cases.

2025-02-16 Diego Morales: Added integration test plan and GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1324 — includes network-chaos harness and golden scenarios for idempotent endpoint flows.
2025-02-18 Product review: PM accepted default conservative approach for non-idempotent ops. PM requested additional docs and migration steps for customers using custom retry logic.
notes_for_engineering: Provide a single cross-language spec (YAML) that each SDK reads to map runtime error codes to semantic classes (RETRYABLE_TRANSIENT, RATE_LIMIT, PERMANENT). This avoids scattered mapping logic.
Keep default surface minimal: expose only 'max_retries', 'initial_backoff_ms', 'max_backoff_ms', 'max_reconnects' and a boolean 'enable_idempotency_header' for enterprise privacy settings.

For streaming: prioritize resume tokens. If server doesn't support resume tokens, client should not attempt byte-range style resume; instead surface clear error recommending application-level idempotency.

Document examples: Python snippet showing with_retry(idempotency_key=uuid4()) for safe generate+commit flows; TS example showing RetryPolicy builder; Go example demonstrating context + idempotency headers.
Telem: send hashed(idempotency_key) using HMAC with SDK-local secret before emitting to telemetry to preserve PII safety.
